# PEN-6188 — correct the stale premise under the broker `image` pin in `buildJobManifest`

PR: [#3563](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/3563), filed from
[PEN-6188](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-6188)

## Files

- `src/server/job-manifest.ts` — comment only, +15/−1

## What changed

Comment text above the broker's image resolution, and nothing else. No rendered
output moves, no behaviour change, no export or signature change. The
`ctx.agent.adapterConfig` resolution PEN-5017 added is untouched; see
[pen-5017.md](./pen-5017.md) for the pin itself.

The corrected sentence read *"the one image value in this function with agent
provenance"*. It now reads *"the one image value in this function that no
OVERLAY can move"*, followed by a block recording why the original was
withdrawn and what carries the other half.

## Why

The original sentence rested on an unstated premise — that the agent row is
operator-controlled, so resolving `image` off it puts the broker's code beyond
an agent's reach. That premise was measured false on 2026-11-08 (PEN-6188):
`agent_config:update` resolves `allow_self` on `PATCH /agents/:id`, so the
subject agent could write its own `adapterConfig`, `image` included — and
`buildJobManifest` hands that value to `buildGitHubPublishBrokerSidecar`, the
container that holds the GitHub push credential at uid 1001.

So the pin was sound against the path PEN-5017 described (a lower SCOPE,
`issue.assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig`, choosing the broker's image)
and silent about a second one (the subject PRINCIPAL writing the agent row the
pin reads). A reader checking "is the broker's image out of an agent's reach?"
against that sentence got a wrong answer from a true-sounding claim. That is
why a comment-only change to vendored source was worth making at all.

## What closes the second path, and where it is not

The write side, server-side, in the same PR: `routes/agents.ts` refuses an
agent-authored write of the pinned `adapterConfig` keys on the agent's own row
(`agentActorUnwritableConfigKeys`, exported from
`server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`).

Nothing in this adapter enforces that, and this entry is not evidence for it.
The two controls are independent and neither subsumes the other: the pin here
stops a lower scope choosing the broker's code; that guard stops the subject
principal choosing it. If the server-side guard is ever removed this comment
stops being true, and nothing in this package will report it — which the
comment now records in place rather than leaving to a reader to notice.
